lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15 from the pinned worktree. Backend: vllm/v1/attention/backends/triton_attn.py; kernel: vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_unified_attention.py; helpers: vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_attention_helpers.py; kv-write: vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py. (1) GRID DECOMPOSITION. Wrapper unified_attention (triton_unified_attention.py:802). GQA group = num_q_heads//num_kv_heads (:929). BLOCK_M = 16 when group<=16, else next_pow2(group) (:932-934); BLOCK_Q = BLOCK_M//group (:935) - so at the host shape (4 KV/rank, d256) BLOCK_M=16 rows pack the whole GQA group; with 32 Q/rank that is 2 decode tokens x 8 heads per CTA (BLOCK_Q=2). Launch-width bound: total_num_q_blocks = q.shape[0]//BLOCK_Q + num_seqs (:966, an upper bound that never needs a CPU sync, comment :957-965). Path select use_3d (:1041-1050): 3D split iff a threshold exists AND max_seqlen_q<=1 (pure decode) AND num_seqs<=threshold AND not VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT. Threshold seq_threshold_3D = MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D//num_kv_heads = 128/4 = 32, then snapped to the nearest CUDA-graph capture size (triton_attn.py:53, 133-152); the comment states the rationale: the 2D grid must reach a minimum launch size of 128 CTAs, so small batches MUST split the sequence instead. Therefore at the host's batch 4-8 the baseline takes the 3D SPLIT path: grid = (total_num_q_blocks, num_kv_heads, 16) (:1081; NUM_PAR_SOFTMAX_SEGMENTS=16, triton_attn.py:54). Concretely: batch 4 -> (4//2+4, 4, 16) = (6,4,16) = 384 CTAs; batch 8 -> (12,4,16) = 768 CTAs, i.e. 2.7-5.3 waves over 72 TU102 SMs at the 2-resident law (144 concurrent). Segment k of 16 covers tiles [k*tiles_per_segment, (k+1)*tiles_per_segment) with tiles_per_segment = cdiv(seq_len, 16*TILE_SIZE) (kernel :322-323; helpers compute_tile_loop_bounds :142-228, IS_3D narrowing :216-220); TILE_SIZE_DECODE = 16 for 2-byte elements (:798-799, :1082), so at ctx2048 each CTA walks 128 KV tokens (8 tiles), at ctx512 32 tokens (2 tiles). Rows beyond the batch exit early (:319-320, segments past seq_len :322-325). The 2D path (num_seqs>threshold or mixed prefill) runs the WHOLE sequence per (q_block, kv_head) CTA with grid (total_num_q_blocks, num_kv_heads) (:1077-1079) - the single-CTA-per-row full online softmax. (2) REDUCTION PLACEMENT. Per tile: S = scale*Q.K^T via tl.dot (:536-542), masked (:547-549), then the standard flash update in softmax_step (helpers :418-440): m_new=max(M,rowmax), P=exp(S-m_new), alpha=exp(M-m_new), L=L*alpha+l_j; acc = acc*alpha + P.V via tl.dot (:561-584). In 3D mode each segment CTA stops after its slice and stores fp32 partials: acc (256-wide) to segm_output[token, head, seg, :], plus per-row (M, L) scalars (:586-642, store_segm_reduce_scalars helpers :242). The cross-segment reduction is a SECOND KERNEL: reduce_segments (:684-771), grid (num_tokens, num_query_heads) (:1169-1170), launched immediately after the walk on the same stream (:1169-1189): loads the 16 maxima, computes overall max, rescales expsums by exp(m_i - M_max), sums rescaled partials, divides, stores the final fp16/quantized output (:729-771). So at batch 4-8 the baseline is ITSELF a split walk + separate combine pair - one CTA per (token, head) finalizes 16 segment partials. (3) LAUNCH COUNT per decode step per full-attention layer: 3 - (a) KV-cache write triton_reshape_and_cache_flash (triton_attn.py:752-795; forward_includes_kv_cache_update=False :316); (b) kernel_unified_attention walk; (c) reduce_segments combine (3D mode only; 2D mode is 2 launches). Rope is separate on CUDA (fused_rope_kvcache_supported -> rocm_aiter only, :797-800). 8 full-attn layers -> 24 attention-kernel launches per step at batch 4-8; the 24 GDN layers do not use this backend. All three launches are captured in CUDA graph - the builder declares AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS (triton_attn.py:100) and use_cascade_attention()=False (:339-340, asserted :575). (4) WORKSPACE. The 3D partials live in persistent builder-allocated buffers (triton_attn.py:154-175): segm_output [seq_threshold_3D, num_heads, 16, 256] fp32 (~16 MiB at 32q/4kv), segm_max/expsum [.,.,16]. No per-step allocation (graph-safe). Round-trip volume actually touched per step = batch*num_q_heads*16*256*4 B = 2 MiB at batch 4, 4 MiB at batch 8 - vs TU102's 5.5 MiB L2, so the write-then-read is largely L2-resident; there is no event or sync between walk and combine. The workspace is thus NOT avoided at the host's batch (only the 2D large-batch path avoids it), but it is L2-scale, not DRAM-scale. (5) THE 50.1 MECHANISM versus the host's split walk+combine pair: the baseline's decode performance decomposes as: (i) CUDA-graph amortization - eager 12.7 -> graphs 50.1 tok/s (3.94x, MEMORY.md 2026-09-09) is the single largest factor, and the backend's code carries the matching discipline (triton_attn.py:577-584 NOTE(woosuk): under piecewise graphs this python runs eager, so views/slices are minimized); (ii) sequence-split x16 to fill 72 SMs at batch<=threshold (the MIN_LAUNCH_GRID_SIZE_2D=128 law, triton_attn.py:133-139) - the same fill lever as the host's PAGES_PER_SPLIT; (iii) whole-GQA-group packing in BLOCK_M=16 so each sequence's KV slice is read exactly ONCE per kv head regardless of q heads (unique KV at batch 4/ctx2048 = 4*2048*4*256*2*2 B ~ 33.5 MiB, ~63 us at 535 GB/s - consistent with the host's ~0.12 ms attention-at-the-wall); (iv) FMA-only tl.dot is SUFFICIENT for it: on sm75 with Triton >=3.3 tl.dot lowers to FMA (host records: headshape/report.md:214, lacunae/SUMMARY.md:17 '3.2's MMAv2 emits native m16n8k8 on cc75; the loss is #5066 in 3.3', CONSOLIDATION.md:220-221), yet the baseline still posts 50.1 - independent confirmation that attention math is not the wall at this shape, the residual vs the host's 41.3/41.2 (0.82) is step-level structure, exactly as host doctrine already concluded (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13: 'the wall moved to DRAM where attention belongs'; 2026-09-14: PROFILE-DELTA lever list EXHAUSTED; short-row mechanism OPEN via chrome-trace). Corollary the host records imply but this read makes concrete: 'second launch' and 'workspace round-trip' cannot alone explain the 4.3 ms - the 50.1 baseline pays both (combine kernel + 2-4 MiB partials) inside its committed number. Number-provenance nuance from the records: 50.1 is the ctx512 row (MEMORY.md 2026-09-09); the champion's ctx2048 row is 41.2 and ctx512 row 41.3, so the like-for-like ratio 0.82 is at ctx512; the task frame's '41.2 vs 50.1' pairs different ctx rows.
lacuna.applicability: Directly transfers: this IS the host's baseline path (TRITON_ATTN control arm per doctrine), so every structural fact above is usable as-is for the step-profile ledger (plan/0010 #step-profile): expected attention graph-node count 24/step at batch 4-8 (3 launches x 8 layers), walk wave count 2.7-5.3, combine grid (batch, q_heads), partial traffic 2-4 MiB L2-resident. The batch-invariance interaction transfers as a caution: setting VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT forces the 2D single-CTA path (triton_unified_attention.py:1049) - upstream's v0.29 batch-invariant matmul tuning (#53247) rides this same switch, so any future determinism experiment silently changes the baseline's kernel structure. Does not transfer: nothing to port INTO the host kernel - the baseline's advantage is not a mechanism the host lacks (it splits, it combines, it round-trips partials); the transferable instrument is the chrome-trace per-kernel diff (MEMORY.md 2026-09-14 named follow-up) to localize where the host's step spends the 4.3 ms the baseline does not (step serialization / gaps, not attention kernel time). The d256 tl.dot FMA-floor caveat (Triton>=3.3) applies to the baseline itself and did not stop 50.1, which lowers the expected value of any 'tensor-core-ize the host walk' proposal on this generation (and the recorded Triton 3.2 escape is a dead end for this family, CONSOLIDATION T10). [uncertain] The exact num_q_heads/rank: task frame gives 4 KV/rank; CONSOLIDATION T7 says 24Q/4KV TOTAL on the 27B (=> 12Q/2KV per rank at TP2, group 6); under EITHER reading BLOCK_M=16/BLOCK_Q=2 and the walk grid are unchanged (group<=16), only the combine grid's head axis (12 vs 32) and partial volume scale.

design.mechanism: Implementable-cold description of the baseline decode path at batch 4-8, ctx 512-2048, 4 KV/rank, d256, fp16 KV: (1) Wrapper: BLOCK_M=16, BLOCK_Q=2, TILE_SIZE=16 (fp16), threshold ~32 (nearest capture size to 128/4). use_3d=True. (2) Walk launch: grid (q_tokens//2 + batch, 4, 16). Program (b, h, s): resolve seq/q-block from cu_seqlens+seq_lens (helpers :45-77); skip if row >= query_len; tiles_per_segment = cdiv(seq_len, 256); tile loop j in [s*tiles_per_segment, min((s+1)*tiles_per_segment, seq tiles)) (causal upper bound = context_len + qpos_hi; helper :181-228). Load Q once (16x256 fp16, :353-373). Per tile: 16 physical block ids from the block table (:424-426); K tile 256x16 and V tile 16x256 gathered by (block_id, kv_head, offset_in_block, dim) strides (:467-491); S = scale * tl.dot(Q, K^T) (:536-542); mask (:547-549); flash step (helpers :418-440) with the -inf-row guard m_j=0; acc = acc*alpha + tl.dot(P, V) (:561-584). (3) 3D epilogue: store acc fp32 to segm_output[token, head, s, :256] and (M, L) to segm_max/segm_expsum (:586-642). (4) Combine launch: reduce_segments grid (batch, q_heads) (:1169): read 16 maxima -> M_max; expsums *= exp(m_i - M_max); out = sum_i(partial_i * exp(m_i - M_max)) / sum(expsums), guarded for zero (:729-771); store final output row (256). (5) Per layer also: reshape_and_cache_flash kv-write kernel (grid from slot count, triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py:427-434). All captured as graph nodes; builder preallocates the segm workspace once (triton_attn.py:154-175).
design.failure_modes: (1) Register pressure at d256: BLOCK_M=16 x 256 fp32 acc + Q tile per CTA is heavy; the host's own kernel hit the 255/254-reg wall at d256 (CONSOLIDATION T2), so the baseline's residency at this shape is not generous; the host's register-accumulator surgery (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13) already mapped this ceiling - replicate its profile-first discipline, not the baseline's layout. (2) FMA-floor tl.dot: on Triton >=3.3 sm75 the two tl.dots are FMA loops (host-recorded #5066 loss; restore PR #9970 closed unmerged 2026-04-09) - measured harmless here (50.1 with FMA attention), but do not copy the baseline's tl.dot shape into a fresh kernel expecting tensor cores. (3) Threshold flips the structure discretely: cross num_seqs>threshold (or set VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT) and the kernel becomes 2D full-sequence walks - comparisons across that boundary compare different kernels; pin capture sizes when benchmarking (the threshold is snapped to capture sizes, triton_attn.py:142-152). (4) The combine divides by total expsum with a zero-guard (reduce_segments :759) - all-masked segments store M=-inf -> exp(-inf)=0, safe, but a segment CTA that exits before storing leaves STALE workspace unless the act_num_segments mask covers it (:723-726); the host's own divergent-barrier bug (MEMORY.md 2026-09-10: per-warp any_alive skip corrupting dims 64+) is the same discipline point: partial-writing collectives must be total. (5) Host falsified levers that rhyme: batching the gather collapsed short decode 78.5% (C1, MEMORY.md 2026-09-10) and KV pipelining was decisively negative at ctx512 (-11.5%, MEMORY.md 2026-09-14) - the baseline's plain strided per-tile gathers with no prefetch stage are consistent with both: at 0.12 ms attention traffic, staging machinery costs more than it hides.
design.effort_estimate: None (read-only item). Feeds plan/0010 #step-profile as pre-localized facts: expected per-layer node count 3, walk waves 2.7-5.3, combine shape (batch, q_heads), partial volume 2-4 MiB L2-resident.
design.priority_signal: MODERATE and load-bearing as an instrument, not as surgery: (1) it falsifies two candidate explanations for the 4.3 ms before any ms is spent - the 50.1 baseline itself pays a second combine launch AND a partials round-trip inside its committed number, so the host's residual cannot be attributed to those alone at L2 scale; the multi-ms search belongs at step level (gaps, serialization, GDN/allreduce interleave) where the outline's graph-node-concurrency and step-roofline-method items and the named chrome-trace follow-up (MEMORY.md 2026-09-14) operate. (2) It hardens the doctrine row: the baseline beats the 41.x champion with FMA-only math on the same silicon - 'close the gap with better attention math' has negative expected value this generation; the ratio 0.82 (ctx512, MEMORY.md 2026-09-13) is structural. (3) It supplies concrete numbers (node counts, wave counts, partial sizes) the step-profile ledger needs to attribute the 4.3 ms without re-deriving them. Against: produces no direct token/s; if the chrome-trace diff lands first, this record is corroboration only.
